clue.text: Let pass

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to allow, as a verb
second meaning: a document granting leave to enter or travel, as a noun

explanation.walkthrough: Read together the words sound like a single instruction to wave something through; they are two separate senses, one a verb and one a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: To allow something is to grant leave, and an official written authorisation is a licence of the same name.

clue.text: It's more obvious when praline crumbles

indicators.note: the sweet crumbles, so its letters break up and re-form

explanation.surface: A confectioner notes that the problem becomes clearer as the nut sweet falls apart.
explanation.definitionFit: The comparative of a word meaning clear or evident describes something easier to see.

clue.text: Medium of our times in Brazilian city

indicators.note: our times sit in the city, inside its letters

parts.note: AD, anno domini, marks the present era

explanation.surface: A modern means of communication found in Rio de Janeiro.
explanation.definitionFit: Broadcasting by sound waves is one of the mass media, a channel of communication.

clue.text: Tim is worried about scheme to introduce, say, hormone into the body

definitions.text: introduce, say, hormone into the body

indicators.note: the worried name goes about, or around, the scheme
a worried name is shaken up, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Tim frets about a medical plan to put hormones into the body.
explanation.definitionFit: Surgeons insert a device or substance into living tissue, the verb sense of this word.

clue.text: Peg put soldier back in place

indicators.note: the reversed soldier is put somewhere, the first half of the insertion instruction
with put, says the soldier goes inside the word for place

parts.note: a spot is a place or location

indicators.note: sending the soldier back means his letters are read in the opposite direction

parts.note: GI is an American private soldier

explanation.surface: An instruction to return a soldier to his post, with a peg as the marker.
explanation.definitionFit: A tap or plug in a cask is a small wooden stopper, a kind of peg driven into the bunghole.

clue.text: Jellyfish, for example, get tumours

definitions.meaning: first meaning: simple sea creatures with a tube body and tentacles, a stage of the jellyfish family
second meaning: small growths on a mucous membrane

explanation.walkthrough: The surface links a sea creature with illness; the word names both a stage of jellyfish life and a medical growth.
explanation.definitionFit: Sea anemones and jellyfish in their fixed stage are tentacled creatures of that name, as are small benign growths in the body.

clue.text: Pop concert organised seat by large storage area

definitions.note: singular phrase for a plural answer: a large capacity of computer memory

parts.note: a gig is a live pop performance

indicators.note: seating that is organised is rearranged, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Seating is arranged next to a big storage space for a rock concert.
explanation.walkthrough: The storage is computer memory, not a warehouse.
explanation.definitionFit: Units of a billion bytes each measure substantial amounts of computer memory.

clue.text: Trial, provided you start to give evidence

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the word whose first letter is taken

explanation.surface: A lawyer tells a witness that, provided they begin, they may speak at the trial.
explanation.definitionFit: A witness states facts under oath in court, which is to bear witness.

clue.text: Claim to be expert on a visit arranged at unrehearsed event

parts.note: I'M PRO, as a person claiming to be a professional would say

indicators.note: the words are arranged anew, so their letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Someone boasts of professional skill at an impromptu gathering laid on for a visit.
explanation.definitionFit: A performance made up on the spot, without preparation, is the definition's sense.

clue.text: Fat landowner lost original inventory

indicators.note: the landowner has lost something, so a letter comes out of his title

parts.note: a laird is a Scottish landowner

indicators.note: the original part of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: the word whose first letter is removed

explanation.surface: A portly landowner has mislaid the first list of his possessions.
explanation.walkthrough: A laird is the owner of a landed estate in Scotland. 'Fat' looks like an adjective for the landowner, but it is the definition, a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Pig fat rendered for cooking is a soft white culinary grease of that name.

clue.text: Its logo is adapted after Briton in Australia is revealed as Apple fan

indicators.note: the reworked logo comes after the Briton, so he goes first

parts.note: Pom is Australian slang for a British person

indicators.note: a logo that is adapted has been altered, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A British expat in Australia, tweaking a company logo, turns out to be a devotee of Apple computers.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital A makes Apple look like the tech firm; the fan is really a student of fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: The science of fruit growing is pomology, so its practitioner is fond of apples in the orchard sense.

clue.text: Greek market place takes in first nanny goat

indicators.note: the market place takes something in, so the letter sits inside it

parts.note: the agora was the public square and market of an ancient Greek city

indicators.note: only the opening letter of nanny is wanted

parts.note: the word whose first letter is taken

explanation.surface: An ancient Greek market first admits a nanny goat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nanny goat' reads as one phrase, but the nanny supplies one letter and the goat is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The Angora is a breed of domestic goat whose long silky hair gives mohair.

clue.text: Government wants some more pub licences

indicators.note: only some of the letters of these words are used, a run lying inside them

parts.note: the run of letters spans the end of more, all of pub and the start of licences

explanation.surface: The authorities would like more licences for pubs to be issued.
explanation.definitionFit: A state ruled by elected representatives rather than a monarch is a form of government.

clue.text: I am involved in prime ITV production about earlier times

definitions.note: an adjectival phrase: belonging to or characteristic of an early stage of development

indicators.note: I am involved in something, so the letter I goes inside the other letters
a production of the words is a reworking of them into a new order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged; ITV is a British television channel

explanation.surface: Someone working on a prime-time ITV programme about history.
explanation.walkthrough: ITV is a British commercial television network, which makes the surface read like a TV credit.
explanation.definitionFit: Primitive means belonging to an early stage of history or development, so it concerns ancient times.

clue.text: Wise men take over skills left by the master

definitions.note: adjectival phrase: produced by or befitting a master

parts.note: the Magi, the three wise men of the Nativity

indicators.note: in a down clue, taking a word over flips it so it reads upward

explanation.surface: The Magi inherit the skills left behind by their teacher.
explanation.definitionFit: This rare adjective means of or befitting a master, authoritative in tone or manner.

clue.text: Support for Guy

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a prop or brace
second meaning: a rope or wire that steadies a mast or tent

explanation.walkthrough: The capital G makes Guy look like a man's name; it is the rope that holds up a tent or mast.
explanation.definitionFit: A brace for a mast is a rope stretched from it, and the same word means anything that props something up.

clue.text: Long story about silver found in South Africa

indicators.note: silver is found in the country, so its symbol sits inside the abbreviation

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: A lengthy tale concerning a silver strike in South Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: A long narrative, originally an Icelandic tale of heroes, is now any drawn-out account.

clue.text: One who boasts the performance has been cancelled?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a braggart who likes to display themselves
second meaning, read as two words: the event is called off

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the whimsical second reading, where the hyphenated noun splits into two plain words.
explanation.definitionFit: A braggart who flaunts their abilities is called this, and an event called off is said to be off.

clue.text: Slanderous that treatment of extrasensory perception varies

indicators.note: a treatment of these letters is a reworking of them into a different order

explanation.surface: A claim that how psychic powers are handled differs from place to place is defamatory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Varies' looks like the anagram signal but is part of the material being rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To cast aspersions is to attack someone's reputation, so this rare adjective means defamatory.

clue.text: Protected information of firm in finished case

definitions.note: an adjectival sense: describes information protected by being put in code

indicators.note: the firm goes in the word for finished
finished forms a case around the firm's letters

explanation.surface: Confidential company details are kept in a closed file.
explanation.definitionFit: Data turned into cipher is secured from prying eyes, which is the sense of this past participle.

clue.text: Talking is not fashionable before sending out requests for payment

indicators.note: the clue says not fashionable, so the fashionable letters are left out

explanation.surface: A remark that chatting about bills is not the done thing.
explanation.definitionFit: Uttering or expressing aloud is speaking, so this present participle means speaking out.

clue.text: Parking offence by minister

parts.note: arson is the crime of setting fire to property

explanation.surface: A clergyman is caught for a parking violation.
explanation.definitionFit: A parish clergyman, especially an Anglican vicar or rector, is a minister of religion.

clue.text: Always the same hypocritical talk about wrong sort of tons

indicators.note: the talk goes about, or around, the other letters
a wrong sort of word has its letters muddled

explanation.surface: Sanctimonious chatter about weighing things by the wrong sort of ton never changes.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unchanging and invariable stays fixed, the sense of this adjective.

clue.text: One who appreciates the work of others

definitions.text: One who appreciates the work of others

parts.note: appreciate here means assess or judge, not enjoy
books, plays or art made by other people, reviewed for a living

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads like praise for a generous admirer, but to appreciate is also to evaluate, which is the reviewer's job.
explanation.definitionFit: A reviewer judges and assesses the merits of other people's books, plays or art.

clue.text: Gerry Adams's supporters question one Middle Easterner

parts.note: the IRA, the Irish Republican Army, linked to Sinn Féin, which Gerry Adams led

explanation.surface: Irish republicans quizzing a man from the Gulf region.
explanation.walkthrough: Gerry Adams was the long-time leader of Sinn Féin, the Irish republican party associated with the IRA.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Baghdad's country is a person from the Middle East.

clue.text: Exchange letters on match

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to write to one another
second meaning: to agree or be equivalent

explanation.walkthrough: In a wordplay puzzle, 'exchange letters' tempts the solver towards swapping letters around; it means writing to someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Pen pals write to each other by post, and two things that agree or tally are said to do likewise.

clue.text: A vote is what the revolution is about

parts.note: a cross on a ballot paper marks a vote

explanation.surface: A political remark that a revolution comes down to a single vote.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests political revolution; the definition means rotation around a central line.
explanation.definitionFit: Anything rotating spins around a central line, so a turning body revolves about it.

clue.text: It's wrong when one sort of fly is circulating

indicators.note: letters that are circulating move about and settle in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone objects to a particular kind of fly buzzing about the room.
explanation.definitionFit: A serious crime in law is a grave wrongdoing, the noun sense of wrong.

clue.text: Moving slowly to the border

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a decorative trim along a margin

explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures someone creeping up to a frontier; 'border' is a separate noun sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Creeping forward gradually is inching, and a trim sewn along a hem is a decorative strip of the same name.
